replication.target_description: Part 1 direct replication of Johnson and Goldstein (2003): consent to organ donation, Opt-Out versus Opt-In, combined direct-replication samples; critical test unresolved between two-sample proportion comparison and Table 6 logistic regression.

n.quote: Replication of Experiment 1 from Johnson & Goldstein (2003) Opt-in default 488 62.5% Opt-out default 476 73.5% No-default (no default) 482 69.7% ... In Part 1, we report the results from 2-sample test for equality of proportions (comparing the participation rate across different defaults). ... Also see Table 6 for the results based on logistic regression.

notes: Only n_r was assigned. All original, replication es/p, and reported_success fields are unassigned placeholders. Identity assessment: supplied text begins with the closely matching title "Defaults versus framing: Revisiting Default Effect and Framing Effect with a replication and extension of Johnson and Goldstein (2003) and Johnson, Bellman, and Lohse (2002)" and contains a primary first-person Methods/Results report, extensive tables and supplementary methods, with matching target studies and project https://osf.io/8wd2b/. This is substantive primary-report text, not an abstract or secondary account. The supplied parse omits the article byline, publication-year header and own DOI; exact author-list/DOI/version identity therefore cannot be independently confirmed from this candidate. No PDF was supplied. The outcome and opt-out versus opt-in contrast are identified, but the supplied description and p.7 locator do not distinguish the reported two-sample proportion test from the three-condition logistic regression. Table 5 provides final, mutually exclusive condition counts. The two-group analytic candidate is 488 + 476 = 964 participants. The three-condition regression candidate is 488 + 476 + 482 = 1446 participants. No single N is assigned while the critical test remains unresolved. The generic N = 1920 includes the temporary-choice extension and is not the direct-replication analytic N. Candidate only: two-group comparison, opt-in 488 + opt-out 476 = 964 participants; three-condition logistic model, opt-in 488 + opt-out 476 + no-default 482 = 1446 participants. Independent direct-replication sample accounting: Sample 1 direct-replication 480 + Sample 2 966 = 1446; Sample 1 temporary extension 474 excluded. The source reports 91 preregistered participant exclusions across the study; per-condition exclusion counts are not supplied.
